long_biography.plain_text:
L.P. Hollander began as a Boston dressmaking business and became a destination for affluent women seeking European fashions. Theodore Hollander and his brothers travelled to London and Paris to source ready-made styles. Their work helped the family firm establish stores on Fifth Avenue and in resort communities from Newport to Palm Beach.

Hollander remained closely tied to the enterprise after its sale, retaining a board position. He also controlled the successor company that held its former leases. His most durable public legacy was the Theodore C. Hollander Trust, created from sale proceeds to support Boston health and education institutions serving newcomers to the city.
